facts.fact_text: Both applicants participated in a number of unauthorised peaceful demonstrations organised by the opposition.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful and were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The demonstration of 11 March 2011 was attended by the second applicant.
The demonstration of 20 October 2012 was attended by both the first applicant and the second applicant.
The demonstration of 17 November 2012 was attended by the first applicant.
In the course of many of those unauthorised peaceful demonstrations, both applicants were arrested and convicted.
Both applicants were arrested during the dispersal operations of the demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted in general terms that the assembly of 17 November 2012 would not be in accordance with the Law on Freedom of Assembly.

In each case following the demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012, the applicants were charged with an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration of 20 October 2012 at the site indicated by the organisers.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration of 17 November 2012.
The organisers decided to hold the demonstrations of 11 March 2011, 20 October 2012, and 17 November 2012 as planned, despite the refusals by the Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA).
According to the first applicant, he was never served with a copy of the administrative-offence report or with other documents from his case file following his arrest on 4 March 2011.
According to the first applicant, he was not given access to a lawyer after his arrest on 4 March 2011 or while he was in police custody.
According to the applicants, they were never served with a copy of the administrative-offence reports or with other documents from their case files following their arrests during the demonstrations.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer after their arrests during the demonstrations or while they were in police custody.

According to the applicants, members of the public were not allowed inside the courtroom during the hearings before the Sabail District Court, even though the court had not taken a formal decision to close the hearings to the public.
According to the applicants, they were not given an opportunity to appoint lawyers of their own choosing at the hearings before the Sabail District Court.
